doc.title: Bobby Watson interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, January 19, 1996

title: Studying with Clifton Williams at Miami
summary: He went to the University of Miami to study with Clifton Williams, who taught him composition through an emotions-on-the-piano test.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Tell us about you know, some of the things you’re saying are fabulous because they’re insights of personal experience that you have as to the sound. But you’ve also studied composition and theory haven’t you? Tell us about your time of study.

Oh, I studied with a man, his name was Clifton Williams. And he is very big in the concert band field. He has several things published. We played them when I was in high school. So when I got a chance to study with him, that’s one of the reasons I went to the University of Miami, was to study with Clifton Williams. And he taught me as a composer, not as a jazz composer. He said, “I want you to be a good composer, so that way, whatever you want to do, whether it be jazz or classical, you will at least have the craft.” And one of the first tests he gave us was he wrote a bunch of emotions, a list, he made — love, hate, boredom, inebriation — a different list of emotions. And anger, fright/fear. And you had to write eight bars, no harmony just the melody. And he said that you would be able to get that across on the piano. He would sit there with his back to the wall and you would pick one. He had a list. And you would just play and he had to guess what it was. And what you had at your disposal was like the rhythmic, how fast it is; the attack; the dynamics; the direction of notes; and that was his test to see if you had a gift for composition. And if you got at least half, you were in the ballpark. That was his method, you know? And that was very exciting for me and I’ve never forgot that and I use that because you know if you’re going to do love say, you want to have a note going down, or pride, that was one of them [scats staccato].
